title: Turn the keyboard backlight on in the dark using the ambient light sensor
head: 5e0a1b974436
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A restarted shell loses the blank-session pause and can relight a locked keyboard
leads.consequence: Pause exists only on the old service instance. If the shell restarts while the lock screen remains blank, the new service starts unpaused, probes the hardware, subscribes to light readings and can set a positive keyboard level after the dark-light settle period, behind the locked screen. There is no lock-state query or replayed pause in startup. The subsequent restore may then overwrite the session receipt or be interpreted as a user change.
leads.triage: matches Opus hypothesis H4 (shell restart while blanked); behavioural edge case, not reproduced; not published

leads.summary: Register iio-sensor-proxy in the ISO offline package list
leads.consequence: On a machine with both devices, install/hardware/ambient-light.sh asks pacman to install iio-sensor-proxy but the offline ISO mirror is populated from the package lists, neither of which includes it. An offline hardware install can therefore fail the package install and leave the light service unavailable. Add iio-sensor-proxy to install/omarchy-other.packages near line 57 (the other open PR #7493 independently adds exactly this entry; reconcile on merge).
leads.triage: factual; verified by coordinator from pinned source; published as N2

leads.summary: A late-discovered ambient sensor exposes a toggle that cannot run
leads.consequence: When the IIO sensor is absent at installation/migration time but appears later, neither guarded one-shot package installation has installed monitor-sensor. The menu's hardware-only when expression nevertheless shows Auto Keyboard Backlight, and its toggle reports enabled, while the service probe declines activation because monitor-sensor is missing. Guard the menu on command availability or provide an install-on-demand path/retry when the sensor appears.
leads.triage: dropped: late-appearing sensor with one-shot install is an edge case consistent with other hardware guards; low value

leads.summary: Open keyboard-backlight PRs claim the same test filename with different test contracts
leads.consequence: PR #12553 and PR #12558 both add test/shell.d/keyboard-backlight-test.sh as a 197-line shell/integration test for persisted brightness; this PR adds the same path as a 127-line Node model test. Whichever path wins a merge, the other feature's test coverage disappears. #12558 additionally adds idle-timeout calls to this PR's pause/resume helper and startup restore behavior, so its merged behavior merits a coordinated check. Rename one test and keep both test suites when merging these PRs.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus section 8; verified via gh; published as related-PR note (corrected: #12558 is stacked on #12553)

flags.claim: Impact: in a dark room, turning the keys off and then locking brings them back on about settleSeconds (5 s by default) after wake
flags.why: The condition was lost. The regression happens only when the service did not step between the key press and the blank (no sensor change and no check timer). With one sensor event after the key press, the off is recorded, held and survives the lock: head, user turns off, then one sensor event gives 0 before the lock and 0 after wake. As written, the sentence reads as unconditional. The 5 s figure is derived from the default settle time (KeyboardBacklightModel.js:11) and was not run at the default. With settle 0.3 s the service wrote 2 about 0.38 s after the restore write.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: added no-sensor-change condition and observed-case result; 5 s described as the default settle time

flags.claim: The service reads the brightness only in step(), which runs when monitor-sensor reports a changed value or a check timer fires
flags.why: As literally stated this is wrong. readBrightness() is also called in start() (Service.qml:77) and resume() (Service.qml:123), and the same paragraph relies on the resume() read ('resume() takes the restored level as its new baseline'). step() is also called from resume() (Service.qml:124). What is true: only step() compares the level against the service's own last write (observeBrightness, Service.qml:88). My report says 'observes', not 'reads'.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: 'checks for a level it did not set itself only in step()'

This is not material: hwmon light reports 'vendor' units (drv-hwmon-light.c:54), which parseLux ignores. The author's own wording is 'six IIO attributes'.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13148#issuecomment-5823991698), checked at `5e0a1b97` after [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13148#issuecomment-5847855479).

**Verified:** all nine earlier points are resolved at `5e0a1b97`. The new pause/resume design adds one regression: a key press the service has not yet seen is discarded at wake. Separately, one packaging gap has been present since the first revision.

| Earlier point | Result at `5e0a1b97` |
|---|---|
| Stale brightness read | Resolved. Under `blockAllReads`, `reload()` then `text()` waits for a fresh read (Quickshell 0.3.1 source). The new service test fails with `blockLoading` put back, and also with the in-flight write skip removed |
| Lock blanking and wake | Resolved when blank and wake come in pairs: `off` pauses before blanking and `restore` resumes after restoring. A run of the unmodified script against `Service.qml` showed no writes while blanked and a fresh decision on wake, in both earlier sequences |
| Comma-decimal locales | Resolved: `LC_ALL=C` on `monitor-sensor`, and `parseLux` accepts a comma |
| Toggle after an early restart | Resolved: `running` is set only through `syncMonitor()`, and the service test's toggle check covers it |
| Sensor detection | Resolved: all six IIO light attributes from iio-sensor-proxy 3.9's udev rules |
| Manual wording, menu guard, timer range | Resolved |
| Service-level test | Resolved: model test 35/35 and service test 8/8 (5 of 5 runs) on the head; the service test fails on `a7e4dc60` |

None of the earlier points needed to be withdrawn.

### A key press made since the last sensor change is lost at wake

The service checks for a level it did not set itself only in `step()`, which runs when `monitor-sensor` reports a changed value or a check timer fires. In a steady dark room neither happens, so a key press is not observed right away. `pause()` does not read the level either, and on wake `resume()` takes the restored level as its new baseline. The key press never becomes a held manual off or a remembered level, and the dark room then turns the old level back on.

Reproduced with the unmodified `omarchy-brightness-keyboard off`/`restore` and the real `Service.qml` (stub `monitor-sensor` with one dark reading and no later changes, synthetic LED, settle time shortened to 0.3 s):

```text
case                              before lock   after wake
5e0a1b97, user turns it off       0             2   (service sets 2 about 0.4 s after restore)
5e0a1b97, user picks level 1      1             2
a7e4dc60, same two cases          0 / 1         0 / 1
5e0a1b97 + change below           0 / 1         0 / 1
```

**Impact:** in a dark room, when the sensor reports no change between the key press and the lock, turning the keys off brings them back on after wake (after the settle time, 5 s by default), and a chosen level is replaced by the old one. With one sensor change in between, the manual off was kept. This contradicts the manual's "stays off until the room has been bright for ten minutes..." and "a brightness you pick is reused". From source (not run), in bright light the result matches the documented "decides again", so the regression concerns dark rooms.

**Suggested change:** observe and persist the current brightness in `pause()`, before setting `paused`, when no write is in flight. At that point `off` has not blanked yet, so the level read is the user's:

```qml
function pause() {
  if (root.active && root.state && !root.paused && !setProcess.running && root.pendingLevel < 0) {
    var before = root.state.manualOffSince
    root.state = KeyboardBacklightModel.observeBrightness(root.state, readBrightness(), Date.now())
    if (root.state.manualOffSince !== before) manualOffFile.setText(root.state.manualOffSince > 0 ? String(root.state.manualOffSince) : "")
  }
  root.paused = true
  checkTimer.stop()
}
```

With this change both cases above keep the user's choice, and the PR's service test still passes (2 of 2 runs).

### `iio-sensor-proxy` is missing from the ISO package list

`install/hardware/ambient-light.sh` installs `iio-sensor-proxy` with `omarchy-pkg-add`, but the package is in neither `install/omarchy-base.packages` nor `install/omarchy-other.packages`. Almost every other package installed by `install/hardware/` scripts (for example `asusctl`, `qmk-hid`, `thermald`, `dell-xps-touchpad-haptics`) is listed in `omarchy-other.packages`, which `docs/file-layout.md` describes as a source for the ISO's offline mirror. This has been the case since the first revision.

**Impact:** on a machine with both a light sensor and a keyboard LED, an offline ISO install can fail to find the package, unless it reaches the mirror some other way (the ISO builder was not checked). `omarchy-pkg-add` then exits 1. `omarchy-apply-hardware` runs with `set -euo pipefail`, so the failed `run_logged` step stops the hardware scripts that follow it in `install/hardware/all.sh`. From source, `omarchy-apply-system` (also `set -euo pipefail`) would then skip its login and post-install steps too.

**Suggested change:** add `iio-sensor-proxy` to `install/omarchy-other.packages`. Open PR #7493 adds the same entry.

**Related open PRs:** #10366 and #12553 (and #12558, which builds on #12553) add their own `test/shell.d/keyboard-backlight-test.sh`, the path of this PR's model test, and change `bin/omarchy-brightness-keyboard`. #12553 rewrites the same `off`/`restore` branch and changes what `restore` puts back, which is the level `resume()` now takes as its baseline.

**Optional test improvement:** two service-test checks do not catch what they target. "its own write is not taken as a manual off" also passes on `a7e4dc60` and with `blockLoading` put back, because the next lit reading clears the phantom off before the check (the bright phase does catch it). "decides again from the light after wake" still passes when `Service.resume()` skips the model's `resume()`. A case with steady dark, a key press to off, `ipc pause`, blank, restore, `ipc resume` and no further sensor lines would cover the regression above.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the changes since `a7e4dc60`, related Omarchy components (lock, idle, `omarchy-system-wake`, `omarchy-shell`) and Quickshell 0.3.1, iio-sensor-proxy 3.9 and brightnessctl source. Isolated runs executed the PR's model and service tests on both heads and on copies with one part of the fix reverted, plus the unmodified `omarchy-brightness-keyboard` against the real `Service.qml` under headless Quickshell 0.3.1, with a stub `monitor-sensor`, a stub `brightnessctl` and a synthetic LED. No real sensor, keyboard backlight, lock screen, suspend or ISO install was used.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
